rationale: A wins because it keeps the live wire visible instead of decorating around it. Its line "the 'now' rests on the launch, not the fight" shows discipline; B's "Priced out of branded weight-loss drugs, patients turn to compounded prescriptions instead" turns a possible access angle into an asserted patient-behavior story without a patient. B has usable bones, but A is the one a founder could use without walking into a public fact-checking exercise.
gaps_in_A: It may be too quick to refuse the access lens entirely: "Patients priced out of branded semaglutide finally have an option" is not publishable as written, but a conditional consumer-health angle could survive if the company can produce a real patient and the real price gap.
"The launch is a material event for a public company" overreaches a little. Public and recently profitable are in the update; materiality is not.
"Story type: funding-mechanics" is the wrong label for the investor angle. This is healthcare equities or risk-reward, not funding mechanics.
gaps_in_B: "Priced out of branded weight-loss drugs, patients turn to compounded prescriptions instead" asserts behavior the update does not prove. No patient, no affordability data, no evidence anyone has turned to Hims for this reason yet.

"Freshly profitable Hims & Hers bets its next act on a drug category regulators are still scrutinizing" duplicates the earlier "A newly profitable Hims & Hers doubles down" regulatory-risk angle. Same protagonist, same tension, different hat.
"betting personalization sells better than price" is invented strategy. The update says at-home blood testing personalizes treatment, not that Hims is repositioning away from price.
"double(s) down" is on the blacklist for a reason. It is business-desk autopilot, not analysis.
